title: Number Complement
description: The complement of a positive integer is the integer you get when you flip all the `0`s to `1`s and all the `1`s to `0`s in its binary representation, starting from its most significant set bit down to bit `0` (ignoring leading zeros). Given a positive integer `num`, return its complement.
hints: Construct a bitmask consisting of all `1`s with the exact same bit length as `num`.
XOR `num` with that mask (`((1 << bit_length) - 1) ^ num`), being careful not to overflow signed 32-bit integers.

examples.explanation: 5 is 101 in binary; flipping every bit gives 010, which is 2.
1 is 1 in binary; flipping it gives 0.
7 is 111 in binary; flipping all bits gives 000, which is 0.
